periods.analysis: Water main breaks are at 13.8 breaks/100mi, under the <=15 target and green. This quarter’s calls clustered on the north pressure zone and two short cast-iron runs near Seabright Avenue, but the count is still in the range I would expect for a coastal system with 1961–1974 cast-iron pipe in the ground. Harborview is growing fast, and the added service connections are not yet showing up as systemwide fragility. The pipes are old, not mysterious.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the current valve-exercise and leak-listening route cadence, with Crew 2 continuing night acoustic runs on the Seabright and Bayshore grids. Use the green result to keep the Pipeline Renewal Program design package for the 1961–1974 cast-iron cohort moving, rather than waiting for the chart to turn ugly. Add asset IDs from each repair ticket to the renewal prioritization table so the budget ask stays tied to evidence.

periods.analysis: The measure moved from 13.8 to 14.2 breaks/100mi, up 0.4 quarter over quarter, but still green against the <=15 target. We had the usual cold-snap stress in December and a few small-diameter failures on CI-68-114 and CI-70-221 near the marina loop. The increase is not a crisis, but it is a nudge from the 1961–1974 cast-iron cohort that corrosion and pressure cycling are doing their work. Our AA-rated financial position helps, but bond ratings do not hold back water under a street.
periods.recommendations: Keep the winter response playbook in place: pre-stage clamps, verify valve maps, and keep the two-callout crew model for nights below 38 degrees. Extend the green-period work by adding pressure logger checks on the marina loop and Old Harbor Road before the next freeze season. Fold the CI-68 and CI-70 repair notes into the Pipeline Renewal Program scoring matrix.

periods.analysis: Water main breaks rose from 14.2 to 14.9 breaks/100mi, a 0.7 increase, and we are still technically green. That is the phrase nobody should get too comfortable with. Repairs this quarter leaned toward 6-inch cast iron installed between 1961 and 1974, especially around the Hillcrest pressure boundary where PRV-3 has been hunting during morning demand. The result remains under the <=15 target, but the trend is now giving us a clean early warning.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the current repair response standard, but add a 60-day pressure-control check on PRV-3, PRV-7, and the Hillcrest boundary valves. Advance Pipeline Renewal Program survey work for the 1961–1974 cast-iron cohort from desktop review to potholing on the top ten ranked segments. Prepare a concise evidence memo for the capital committee showing the movement from 13.8 to 14.2 to 14.9 breaks/100mi.

periods.analysis: The measure crossed into yellow at 15.6 breaks/100mi, up 0.7 from 14.9 and now above the <=15 target. This is the quarter where the trend stopped being background noise. We saw repeat repairs on asset IDs CI-66-032 and CI-72-408, both in the 1961–1974 cast-iron cohort, with failures after high weekend demand on the beach route. The system is dependable overall, but this particular pipe cohort is making its condition known.
periods.recommendations: Treat 15.6 breaks/100mi as the watch item and run a weekly break review until the rate moves back below 15. Prioritize Pipeline Renewal Program design for CI-66-032, CI-72-408, and adjacent cast-iron segments before adding lower-risk streets to the bid set. Keep crews on the beach-route flushing and pressure-monitoring schedule through summer, because demand swings are part of the load case.

periods.analysis: 16.3 breaks per 100 miles this quarter, against a target of 15. The deterioration is concentrated in the 1961–1974 cast-iron cohort on the northwest grid; crews closed 118 repairs with average restoration at 5.2 hours. Pipeline Renewal phase 2 (Maple St corridor) is the active mitigation.
periods.recommendations: Keep the yellow watch active and set a trigger: any additional repeat failure on Harborview Boulevard should move that segment to immediate Pipeline Renewal Program construction packaging. Extend the useful green-era practices by maintaining Yard B clamp stock, after-hours locator coverage, and the weekly GIS cleanup of repair tickets. Direct engineering to complete 60 percent plans for the west reservoir feed replacement before Q4 procurement.

periods.analysis: 17.0 breaks per 100 miles — first red quarter. The cast-iron cohort is failing faster than the replacement schedule assumed. Maple St corridor replacement completed this quarter, which removes roughly 0.8 breaks/100mi from the forward run rate. Requesting the phase 3 condition survey be pulled forward.
periods.recommendations: Shift the first Pipeline Renewal Program package for the 1961–1974 cast-iron cohort into accelerated bid review, starting with Harborview Boulevard, Hillcrest boundary, and the marina loop. Maintain emergency response coverage with one dedicated water crew and one standby excavation contractor through winter. Report weekly on breaks/100mi, repeat-failure asset IDs, and restoration backlog until the red condition is under control.

periods.analysis: 18.0 breaks per 100 miles, second consecutive red quarter. The Maple St outage in March was a 10-hour restoration affecting 600 households — the visible cost of the cohort problem. Phase 3 contractor procurement is complete; the pipe-cohort condition survey is next. The pipes don't care about our fiscal year; the funding request shouldn't wait for it either.
periods.recommendations: Keep the Pipeline Renewal Program in incident-command mode for the red measure: weekly construction coordination, open-cut permit tracking, and direct linkage from each break ticket to the renewal priority list. Add a second leak-detection vendor for the north and west pressure zones so we are not waiting on one calendar. Hold the emergency repair contract capacity through the rainy season and do not release standby crews until the rate flattens.

periods.analysis: June closed at 19 water-main breaks per 100 miles, above the target of 15. The cast-iron 1961–74 cohort accounted for 13 of those breaks; that concentration gives the renewal survey a practical starting point.
periods.recommendations: Keep the cast-iron cohort on the priority survey list and compare its break history with the Phase 3 condition findings before selecting replacement segments.
